focus_areas: Limb digit separation and anatomical correctness

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the hind feet. AI often struggles with digit separation in heavy animals. Check if the toes are distinct or if they merge into a stump. Also, verify that the frill's connection to the neck looks physically robust and not just pasted on.
image_description: A side-profile view of a Triceratops dinosaur model or rendering against a white background. The subject is dark grey/black with yellowish striping on the back and frill edge. It exhibits the characteristic large bony frill, three horns (two brow, one nasal), and a parrot-like beak. The body is quadrupedal with thick, columnar limbs and textured skin resembling scales.

expert_testimonies.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out other ceratopsians (e.g., Torosaurus, Styracosaurus) based on frill and horn morphology.
To verify the continuity of the skin texture and ensure the frill is structurally connected to the skull without melting or floating artifacts.
To assess the overall realism of the texture mapping and identify any subtle generation artifacts like noise or inconsistent lighting.
